## TL;DR

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.109 removed the `efficiency` Auto tier that RepoOS used as the default for `github copilot`. The agent connectivity test and every engineering run failed before any prompt reached the model. This change centralizes Auto tier resolution in `src/core/copilot-auto-tier.ts`, maps `default` and the legacy `copilot-auto-efficiency` model id to `--auto-tier balance`, improves failure text when the CLI rejects a tier, and updates docs and compatibility metadata. No live tier probe was added at agent-test time; tier ids remain account-specific and are documented instead.

## Work and rationale

The regression was immediate and total: Copilot validates `--auto-tier` against the signed-in account catalog before running a prompt, so every RepoOS invocation that still passed `efficiency` exited with a clear CLI message while `stderr` was otherwise unhelpful in Settings. RepoOS had two independent mappings—`modelArgs` in `src/server/agents.ts` and `modelArgs` on the contract template in `src/core/agent-contract.ts`—both hard-coded `efficiency` for `default` and `copilot-auto-efficiency`.

Consolidating into `copilot-auto-tier.ts` keeps a single source of truth for which RepoOS model ids select Auto mode and which CLI tier string they emit. `resolveCopilotAutoTier` maps `default`, empty model, `copilot-auto-efficiency`, and `copilot-auto-balance` to `balance`; `copilot-auto-intelligence` maps to `intelligence`; any other id is treated as a named Copilot model and passes through as `--model <id>` only. That preserves saved configs that still reference `copilot-auto-efficiency` while fixing the default runtime behavior.

`formatCopilotAutoTierFailure` hooks into `oneShotFailureDetail`, which already normalizes agent and Settings test failures from stderr or structured stdout. When Copilot’s text matches tier/catalog failure patterns, RepoOS replaces the raw CLI line with guidance that names the rejected tier (when parseable), quotes tier ids from the CLI’s own “Set --auto-tier to …” suggestion when present, and otherwise points users at Balance and Intelligence without asserting a closed global catalog. That satisfies the requirement not to hard-code tiers as the only valid set while still giving actionable copy on the Agents page.

The Settings store label for `copilot-auto-efficiency` was updated to “Auto · Balance” so the UI matches behavior. `src/core/models.ts` already exposed Balance and Intelligence in the Agents dropdown; no interactive `/model` picker list was added because exact `--model` ids for named models are unverified. `agent-compatibility.json` notes the mapping change in verification text and upgrade guidance.

Acceptance criterion three asked for an optional one-prompt probe at agent test time to learn which tier an account accepts. That would spend Copilot credits on every Settings test and race account policy changes; mapping to Balance as the documented successor to Efficiency plus parsing CLI suggestions on failure was judged sufficient. `user-docs/agents.md` and `docs/architecture.md` document account-specific catalogs and the efficiency retirement.

## Approaches tried

The first fix path considered was renaming the default model id from `copilot-auto-efficiency` to `copilot-auto-balance` everywhere. That would have broken persisted overrides, budget allowlists, and probe pins that still store the old id. Keeping the id as an alias that resolves to `balance` at argv build time avoids migration churn while making new defaults correct.

Inlining tier logic only in `agents.ts` was rejected because the agent contract certifier and `repoos doctor` probes use `COPILOT_CONTRACT.modelArgs`; duplicating the map had caused the original drift. A shared module imported by both server drivers and contract templates prevents recurrence.

A closed enum of valid tiers in code was avoided. The formatter prefers tier names extracted from the live error string; only when the CLI omits suggestions does the message mention Balance and Intelligence as common examples with a pointer to `copilot --help`.

## Challenges and blockers

No non-interactive Copilot command lists Auto tiers for an account; validation only appears on failure. Live verification of `--auto-tier balance` on the task author’s account was not run in this managed turn (credit cost and sandbox network). Human confirmation on a real `copilot` binary remains the practical post-merge check.

The previous agent turn ended with a network error before handoff; implementation was already committed on the branch when this turn resumed. Remaining work was scoped check, engineering report, and handoff request.

## Key learnings

Copilot’s Auto tiers are product configuration surfaced as CLI preference ids, not stable ABI. RepoOS model ids for harness defaults can outlive vendor catalog changes; alias ids with comments and compatibility notes are cheaper than wide config migrations.

Agent failure surfaces should parse vendor errors when they embed remediation (tier suggestions) instead of freezing a second catalog in RepoOS. Centralizing harness-specific argv shaping in `src/core` modules that both runtime and contract tests import is worth the extra file for any flag that appears in more than one call site.

Tests cover tier argv mapping and `oneShotFailureDetail` rewriting via `agent-drivers.test.ts` without network. A dedicated unit file for `formatCopilotAutoTierFailure` edge cases could be added later; table-driven cases in the driver suite were enough for review scope.
